rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-year (2018-2019) replicated field experiments at Zhengzhou and TandoJam with measured soil water, N, LAI, dry matter and yield, plus WHCNS model calibrated (2018) and validated (2019). Q2: Section 3.2/3.3 and Table 4 - at Zhengzhou, drip (DI) used 45 mm irrigation vs 120 mm under flood (FI), i.e. 62.5% less water (metered), and WUE was 3.4 and 3.2 kg m-3 under DI vs 2.6 and 2.7 under FI; order of WUE was DI > FI > RF. Q4: Table 4 and Section 3.3 - the model (validated against measured soil water content) partitions ET, showing FI evaporation 195.9 mm vs 147.0 mm under DI (33% higher) with nearly equal transpiration, and FI drainage ~20 mm vs ~1 mm under DI; conclusions state DI conserved water by decreasing evaporation, drainage and runoff.
rows.notes: Drip vs flood compared only at the Zhengzhou site (one soil, one crop, one climate; 130 m2 plots); TandoJam compared flood deficit levels only. WUE uses measured yield but simulated ET; no second independent method, so Q3 no. No explicit limitations, no required conditions stated from own findings (cost barrier to drip in TandoJam is cited from Tunio et al.), and no SD/CI for WUE or water saving; model RMSE/d/r values do not count for Q9.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own replicated two-year field experiments with measured grain yield (harvested at <15% grain moisture), LAI and dry matter. Q2: Section 3.2 and Fig. 3 - at Zhengzhou, DI produced a significantly (p<0.05) higher two-year total grain yield of 22,449 kg ha-1 vs 20,434 under flood FI, a 9.8% increase; Conclusions state DI would significantly improve yield compared with farmer flood practice. Q4: Sections 2.3, 3.1, 3.3 and Table 4 - root-zone soil water content (0-80 cm) was measured weekly in each plot, LAI and dry matter measured at growth stages, and the model partitioned evaporation/drainage, with the yield gain attributed to vigorous growth under optimal root-zone water and higher biomass accumulation (Fig. S1).
rows.notes: Yield advantage of drip over flood is from a single site (Zhengzhou, sandy clay loam, maize Luobai-3), plot scale; measured and simulated yields are not independent since the model was calibrated on the yield data (r=1). Significance only via p<0.05/LSD; no SD, SE or CI reported in the text for yield. No stated limitations and no own-finding conditions for the yield effect (the mechanism statement about optimal root-zone water cites El-Hendawy et al.).

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Fig. S1 supplementary not available; whether Fig. 3 includes error bars cannot be verified from the text.
